//: Where every committed markup fixture came from, and under what licence. The corpus is committed rather than fetched so the suite is hermetic: CI needs this repository and nothing else.

ok.note: Well-formed markup, written to cover every construct the parser branches on: implied end tags, tables, every attribute shape, every character reference shape, raw text, comments, custom elements, and the whitespace cases the printer has to leave alone.

broken.note: Deliberately invalid markup, one construct per file: unclosed elements, stray end tags, EOF inside a tag and inside a comment, duplicate attributes, bogus comments, malformed character references, CDATA in HTML, a late doctype, end tags for void elements, the adoption-agency case, the attribute-value edges where an unquoted value meets `/>`, and a `<?php ?>` processing instruction, which HTML does not have and reads as a comment.

foreign.note: SVG and MathML, including the four places where the same bytes mean different things: `/>`, attribute case, CDATA, and `<title>`. Also the integration points, where HTML comes back into scope.

shrub.note: Shrubbery HTML written by hand, covering every construct the syntax can spell.

html5lib.note: The tokenizer suite: each case an input and the token stream the specification says it produces. The only vendored EXPECTED ANSWERS in this repository -- everything else is either computed from a reference or compared against the library itself. `xmlViolation.test` is excluded: it tests a serialisation policy rather than the tokenizer. The tree-construction tests that used to live alongside these moved to web-platform-tests and are no longer in that repository, which is why `conform` uses a parser rather than a corpus.

borrowed.//: Two corpora already in this repository are used as adversarial input for `survive`, and cost nothing: almost none of either is markup, so both exercise recovery paths the authored corpus never reaches.
borrowed.notation: test/corpus -- 696 shrubbery files, the notation's own differential suite
borrowed.css: test/css/corpus -- 347 CSS files, the CSS module's own suite

reference.//: The `conform` oracle's external reference is a MoonBit dependency rather than a corpus: `moonbit-community/html@0.2.1`, a conforming WHATWG parser, declared in the ROOT module's moon.mod and nowhere else. `tools/boundary-check.sh` gates that. Nothing needs fetching at test time, so the suite stays hermetic.
reference.//divergences: Where the reference and this library disagree, the tie-break was Chromium's DOMParser rather than an assertion. test/html-oracle-policy.json names every file that does not conform and says whose divergence it is.

pending.//: The vendored suites that belong here and are not here yet. Each is MIT and each would be committed under its own bucket with its provenance recorded above, exactly as `test/css/corpus` does.
pending.biome: crates/biome_html_parser/tests -- the ok and error suites.
pending.prettier: Prettier's HTML specs, as vendored by biome.
pending.//how: Adding them is mechanical: drop the files into a new bucket directory, record the count and licence above, and add a floor per bucket to test/html-oracle-policy.json. The oracles need no change.

excluded.scraped-pages: A real page copied from the web has unclear provenance, and a corpus that cannot be relicensed is a corpus that cannot be published. The same call test/css/corpus/manifest.json makes about lightningcss, for a different reason.
